 UAE announces Eid Al Etihad 2026 holidays, federal employees to get five-day break
 Anjum Khan • | 16 November 2026 Unlike federal government employees, private-sector workers will have Friday, 4 December, as a regular working day. 
 The UAE has announced public holiday arrangements for the country's 55th Eid Al Etihad, with federal government employees set to receive a three-day break and private-sector employees entitled to two days of paid leave in December 2026.
 According to the UAE Government Media Office, the holiday for federal government employees will run from Wednesday, December 2, to Friday, December 4. With the regular Saturday-Sunday weekend, employees will enjoy five consecutive days off before returning to work on Monday, December 7.
 For private-sector employees, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) has confirmed Wednesday, December 2, and Thursday, December 3, as paid public holidays. 
 The ministry announced the dates on November 13, confirming that the two-day holiday will apply to employees of private-sector establishments across the country.
 Unlike federal government employees, private-sector workers will have Friday, December 4, as a regular working day.  
 However, those with sufficient annual leave could extend their break by taking additional days off.
 Eid Al Etihad, observed annually on December 2, commemorates the founding of the United Arab Emirates in 1971, when six emirates came together to form the federation. Ras Al Khaimah joined the union in 1972.
 The national occasion celebrates the country's unity, identity and development, while honouring the vision of its founding fathers, led by the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan.
 The 55th Eid Al Etihad celebrations will take place during the UAE's Year of Family, with this year's theme highlighting the role of families, generations and communities in shaping the country over the past 55 years.
 The theme presents the UAE as a "family of families", bringing together people from diverse backgrounds through shared values, experiences and a sense of belonging.
 Families and communities across the country are being encouraged to participate in the national celebrations and mark the anniversary.
